endorsements.quote: We propose the following best practices to ensure FAIR reporting of preprocessing steps in clinical informatics:

We encourage researchers in clinical informatics to integrate in their pipelines DMPs, and we suggest international conferences and journals to enforce sharing the DMP’s link, together with code and dataset’s repository if applicable, detailing preprocessing steps and data provenance with the public code in persistent identifiers.
Separating an independent subset of the data for testing the model at the beginning of the project 9 .

unlisted_practices: Authors should document all data preprocessing steps (data splitting, label adaptation, format conversion, annotation and feature selection, normalization, augmentation) in the main text and supplementary materials, since releasing code alone does not guarantee reproducibility.
Researchers should preserve and archive preprocessing methods, tools, conversions and metadata in a long-term registry or repository with standardized metadata.
Researchers should record metadata changes and data provenance after preprocessing to ensure traceability.
Researchers should use standard, well-identified and versioned preprocessing tools and report their internal parameters in metadata.
Researchers should report the HU window and preserve original device, acquisition and metadata information when converting DICOM to other image formats.
Researchers should apply data augmentation and resampling only to training data, not to validation or test data, and state this explicitly.
Journals and conferences should enforce preprocessing reporting best practices through submission guidelines.
Researchers should describe how ground-truth labels were derived from multiple readers and discuss label uncertainty, noise and edge cases.
Researchers should describe data for auditing, planned quality control tests, and measures to identify data and concept drift in clinical deployment.
Researchers should use machine-readable metadata schemas such as Croissant, FAIR4ML and FAIR4prep to document datasets and preprocessing pipelines.

screen.reason: The paper proposes a framework and reporting standard (FAIR4prep) for documenting clinical informatics data preprocessing rather than conducting an empirical evaluation of an AI tool.
